sourceNote: Reviewed all supplied events E0–E2601. The transcript contains substantial transcription errors, interruptions, and speaker changes within individual events. Attribution follows conversational context; U marks inseparably mixed events or unresolved boundaries. No edited teaser replays were identified. No episode clearly met the unsupported-slogan or explicit criticism-protection criteria: the disputed conclusions occur within extended arguments, and weaknesses in those arguments alone do not establish slogan substitution.

contrasts.speaker: A
contrasts.quote: I'm not saying we've got empirical refutation of any principles of classical object
contrasts.explanation: A supports his analogy with the development of non-Euclidean geometry and evidence of curvature, then expressly limits its application to logic at E2469–2478. He distinguishes an available conceptual alternative from an empirical refutation, rather than treating the analogy as conclusive proof.

contrasts.speaker: B
contrasts.quote: it's always going to be fallible
contrasts.explanation: B explicitly concedes at E991–1001 that theism does not ensure better experimental results. He then distinguishes particular experimental success from justification of general regularity at E1002–1020. Whether that distinction answers A is disputed, but the qualification does not promise an unfailing test or dismiss contrary results automatically.
